messages:
Elliot Price: Heads up — we’re in the publish window for the security enablement kit pages today/tomorrow. Want to sync on (1) Confluence publish mechanics (canonical + permissions) and (2) public-doc link hygiene so the FAQ/RFP library points at stable URLs. Can folks confirm owners + any last edits?

Wei Chen: I can take public docs link hygiene. I saw in the draft FAQ some links pointing to old redwood-docs paths (and a couple to internal Confluence). We should make sure *customer-facing* docs only point to public pages + the “request evidence via GRC” flow, not the internal evidence index.

Kira Thompson: +1. Also we need to avoid linking directly to Drive PDFs from docs-site (those URLs churn + permissions). Confluence should be canonical for internal/field, and public docs should be separate safe subset.

Naomi Feldman: Confirmed. Confluence is canonical source of truth for Security FAQ v2 + one-pagers; Drive PDFs are packaging only. For public docs we’ll only expose the high-level “Security FAQ (public)” page and generic security overview pages. Anything evidence-related stays behind the Customer Security Review Process SOP.

Elliot Price: Great. For Confluence publishing: I’m planning to:
- Move the Security FAQ v2 + one-pagers under Sales Enablement > Security Enablement Kit (space)
- Apply “Customer-shareable” label to the pages we export as PDFs
- Keep the evidence SOP page restricted to Security & Compliance space only (no cross-links from customer-shareable pages)
- Add footer “Last reviewed” + owner and a short “Hosted/Dedicated/Private” banner.

Soojin Lee: Re: formatting — DES template has the footer stamp; I’ll double-check it’s applied consistently. For PDFs: please keep the same footer version string as the Confluence page so field can screenshot.

Wei Chen: Quick question: do we want a single public docs landing link we can reference in the customer-shareable materials? Something like https://docs.redwood.ai/security or https://docs.redwood.ai/security/overview

Elliot Price: Yes. For now, use https://docs.redwood.ai/security (we can redirect later). I’ll make sure internal pages don’t hardcode the old /docs/security-overview path.

Marcus Lin: On the audit logging one-pager, there was a nit: the draft says “exports to SIEM via webhook” — but today it’s “export via HTTPS endpoint / scheduled delivery” depending on deployment mode. Please make sure docs don’t claim a specific mechanism unless it’s in product.

Kira Thompson: I can update that language on the Confluence one-pager. For public docs, we should keep it generic: “export supported; details available on request / depends on deployment.”

Wei Chen: I’m in PR_4821 now (redwood-docs). It touches security overview + deployment mode boundary + audit logs overview. I’ll align phrasing with the approved FAQ:
- Avoid “always/never”
- Use “by default” + “configurable options available”
- Explicit Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private shared responsibility.

Olga Petrov: Please also add a small callout in the public docs that SOC 2 report is available under NDA and must be requested through our evidence process. We should not host reports or pen test summaries publicly.

Wei Chen: Ack. I’ll add a “Requesting compliance evidence” section with contact guidance (security@redwood.ai?) + “your AE/SE can coordinate.” Is security@ ok to publish?

Naomi Feldman: Use “security@redwoodinference.com” for external, and in internal Confluence we can mention the intake alias + the SOP page. (Don’t put the internal alias on public docs.)

Ethan Park: For SSO page link targets: current public docs are at /platform/auth/sso (but it’s thin). If we’re referencing SAML/SCIM, make sure we don’t say SCIM is GA unless we’re confident.

Kira Thompson: Agree — internal one-pager can say “SCIM available for eligible enterprise plans (contact us)” but public docs should say “SCIM may be available” and avoid timeline promises.

Elliot Price: Concrete to-dos:
1) @Kira Thompson update Confluence audit logging one-pager wording (export mechanisms + what’s logged) + verify Hosted/Dedicated/Private table.
2) @Wei Chen update PR_4821 with corrected link targets + generic evidence request section + remove any Confluence links.
3) @Soojin Lee verify formatting/footer + version stamp template.
4) I’ll publish Confluence pages once Naomi signs off on final wording.

Wei Chen: On link hygiene: can we standardize on relative links in docs site where possible? Example: use /security and /platform/auth/sso vs full https URLs.

Elliot Price: Yes, do relative inside docs. For Confluence/Drive, use full URLs (but don’t point to Drive from public docs).

Marcus Lin: Also check we’re not leaking internal event names in public docs. Some customers ask for sample audit events; we can provide via support under NDA, but public should keep categories.

Wei Chen: Got it. I’ll remove concrete event names from the public page and keep “event categories” only.

Naomi Feldman: While you’re in there: please ensure the deployment boundary language matches the security FAQ v2 (especially Private: customer-managed networking + keys when using customer KMS/HSM; Redwood manages control plane components per agreement). No absolutes.

Kira Thompson: Update pushed on the Confluence draft for audit logging + retention cross-link. I left a comment where retention mentions “30 days” — we should phrase as “default retention period varies by deployment and configuration; details in retention one-pager.”

Olga Petrov: Yes please. Do not hardcode a single number in the FAQ; customers read it as a commitment.

Elliot Price: :thumbsup: I’ll scrub for numbers and convert to “default + configurable” language with “contact us” where required.

Wei Chen: PR_4821 updated. I added:
- /security landing stub
- Evidence request section (SOC 2 under NDA)
- Updated audit logging language (“export options available; depends on deployment”) and removed event names.
Ready for review from @Naomi Feldman and @Marcus Lin.

Marcus Lin: Reviewing now.

Ethan Park: I checked the SSO section in the doc changes — looks fine. The only tweak: say “SAML 2.0 SSO supported” and “SCIM provisioning may be available for enterprise” (no guarantees). :+1:

Soojin Lee: Formatting check: footer stamp consistent on the one-pager templates. Just make sure the PDF export includes the same “Last reviewed: 2026-02” line as the Confluence page. (Confluence macros sometimes drop during export.)

Elliot Price: Good call. I’ll do a test export and verify.

Naomi Feldman: Reviewed PR_4821 — looks aligned. One edit request: change “SOC 2 Type II compliant” to “Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report” (we avoid “compliant” language). Once that’s in, I’m good.

Wei Chen: Updated wording and pushed.

Marcus Lin: Approved from SecEng side. Thanks for removing the event names.

Elliot Price: Awesome. I’m publishing the Confluence pages now (customer-shareable labeled), then generating PDFs to Drive. I’ll post final links in #sales once live. Please keep an eye out for any broken links in the FAQ after publish (Confluence sometimes rewrites anchors).

Olga Petrov: Thanks — once you post final links, I’ll update the evidence SOP with “what’s public vs customer-shareable” guidance so we don’t accidentally attach internal docs.

Elliot Price: Perfect. Closing the loop after publish + export.
